original_question: Determine whether a starvation-driven switch between foraging and home attraction can generate nontrivial spatiotemporal dynamics or patterns, whether such switching helps or harms the species biologically, and what alternative satisfaction measures can drive similar behavioral modification.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 37 in Section 2.5 (Learning), for the newly proposed one-dimensional model (2.38) based on the satisfaction measure s(x,t)=m(x,t)/u(x,t) from (2.36) and the switching rule (2.37). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the three substantive parts of the paper's official question: whether the starvation-driven switch between foraging and home attraction in model (2.38) can create nontrivial spatiotemporal dynamics or patterns, whether such switching benefits or impairs the species biologically, and what other satisfaction measures could serve as behaviour-modification mechanisms. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
missing_details: The paper ties this question specifically to the newly proposed local one-dimensional PDE model (2.38) in Section 2.5, not to a general class of switching or foraging-home-attraction systems. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The unknown is the forager population density u(x,t); the model also involves the local resource density m(x,t), a central den location x0 in the spatial domain Ω, a diffusion coefficient d, and home-attraction strength gamma. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The actual model is ∂u/∂t = ∂/∂x(d ∂u/∂x - u ∂/∂x(omega_tilde(s)m + gamma|x-x0|)), with 0 < gamma < gamma_plus, so that movement toward resources takes priority only when hunger is high. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The switch is governed by the satisfaction/starvation measure s(x,t)=m(x,t)/u(x,t) from (2.36), together with the advection rule omega_tilde(s)=gamma_plus for 0 ≤ s < 1 and omega_tilde(s)=0 for 1 ≤ s < ∞ from (2.37); when s<1 the resource-attraction term is 'on,' and when s≥1 the default den attraction dominates. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

A paper-faithful stand-alone version should note that adding nonlocal perception is not part of this question; that is separated out as Open Problem 36. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The nearby context explicitly suggests one alternative satisfaction measure, namely s(x,t)=m(x,t)/m(t), where m(t) is the average resource density at time t; depending on the chosen composite advection law omega(s), the advection speed may increase, decrease, or even change sign. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The paper does not fix initial data, boundary conditions, or a single formal biological objective inside Open Problem 37 itself; later Section 4.2 explains that biological 'success' is context-dependent and may be assessed by persistence/survival or by foraging-based measures, so the refined question should not hard-wire a success metric not chosen in the paper. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

Algebraic data such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, or nilpotency conditions are not part of this paper's formulation; the missing stand-alone details are instead the PDE, its variables, coefficients, and switching law. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
refined_question:
For the newly proposed local one-dimensional model
∂u/∂t = ∂/∂x(d ∂u/∂x - u ∂/∂x(omega_tilde(s(x,t)) m(x,t) + gamma|x-x0|)),
where u(x,t) is the forager density on a one-dimensional domain Ω, m(x,t) is the local resource density, x0∈Ω is a central den site, 0 < gamma < gamma_plus, s(x,t)=m(x,t)/u(x,t), and omega_tilde(s)=gamma_plus for 0 ≤ s < 1 and omega_tilde(s)=0 for 1 ≤ s < ∞ so that hungry foragers prioritize resource attraction while otherwise defaulting to home attraction, determine whether this starvation-driven switching mechanism can generate nontrivial spatiotemporal dynamics or pattern formation, whether such switching is biologically beneficial or detrimental to the species, and whether other satisfaction measures—especially the alternative s(x,t)=m(x,t)/m(t), with m(t) the average resource density at time t—can serve as comparable behaviour-modification mechanisms in the same modelling framework. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Open Problem 37, rather than of the adjacent Open Problems 35 or 36 or the later Section 4 measures-of-success questions. In Section 2.5, the paper first introduces learning through satisfaction measures, defines s(x,t)=m(x,t)/u(x,t) in (2.36), introduces the on/off advection rule (2.37), and then formulates the den-site model (2.38). Immediately after that, Open Problem 37 asks whether the starvation-driven switch between foraging and home attraction can produce nontrivial spatiotemporal dynamics and patterns, whether such realistic switches benefit or impair the species biologically, and what other satisfaction measures could act as a behaviour-modification mechanism. The nearby paragraph explicitly proposes s(x,t)=m(x,t)/m(t) as an alternative satisfaction measure. Section 4.2 later clarifies that biological success is context-dependent, so the refined question should preserve the paper's biological clause without replacing it by a stronger or different formal objective. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
